# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 93 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 93 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_093_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — The Round Stone and Wealth

**1** "What about the speckled stones that were thrown out?" I asked. **2** "These are the wavering ones," he said, "neither truly alive nor truly dead. They're similar in character to the cracked-mountain people, but worse — they make solemn oaths and then lie. That's why they're speckled: oath-breaking tangled with dishonesty has corrupted the very fabric of their faith." **3** "And the short ones?" "These believed and were mostly upright people — but there was a streak of malice in them, which kept them short and not fully healthy. Many of them can still be saved if they turn around quickly." **4** "What about those half-white and half-black?" **5** "These are people consumed by business who never really connect with other believers — that's why they're half-alive. **6** Their preoccupation with work and distraction was so total that some of them managed to repent and find rescue; others were completely lost — they couldn't commit to either the living or the dead. These are the double-minded." **7** "Now those white, round stones that wouldn't fit the tower — who are they?" I asked. **8** "How long are you going to keep being dense?" he said. "These are people of faith who also have great worldly wealth. When hardship comes, they deny their Lord because of their money and their business dealings." **9** "So when will they ever fit the tower, Lord?" "When their wealth — the thing that keeps leading their souls astray — gets stripped away from them," he said. "Then they'll be useful to God. Think of it this way: a round stone can only become square if it's cut — something has to be taken from it. In the same way, the wealthy can only become useful to God when their wealth gets cut away from them."

---

*PNEUMA makes the wealth critique explicit and accessible: money is not merely a distraction but a structural impediment to kingdom-fitness, requiring painful removal.*
